content: The flexibleLinter is really useful, I keep it active on everything I do. However I work in projects which use a tactic from Aeneas for closing goals that often follows simp. It's very much a flexible tactic and so it is reasonable to permit this pattern without warnings. Would it be reasonable and useful to be able to add this tactic to the flexible list for flexibleLinter? I'm happy to do the work if this generally seems a good idea. @Damiano Testa?
Maybe it would be nice if this were extensible so that downstream projects can add whichever tactics they would like to consider flexible.
Yes! This is what I had in mind: an option to specify in the lakefile (or elsewhere) in the project which imports mathlib, the desired customisation.

This is certainly something that could be added: I think that the unusedTactic linter can dynamically add new tactics that are "expected" to do nothing.

For instance, when I am teaching, I like using done to end a proof and I do not want the linter to tell me that done does nothing, nor do I want to silence the linter on every teaching file that I have.
However, the flexible tactic linter has various internal distinctions of how to track which tactic, and I do not know how many of these distinctions are important in downstream projects.

Allowing a tactic to be considered flexible can be relatively straightforward: move the current list of flexible tactics from being an internal definition, to something stored in an environment extension that the linter can access and the users can modify.

I can see this working well for tactics like aesop. The main issue here is that there is no aesop only version that should be considered a stopper (or normalising) tactic that can be preceded by a flexible one, and can be followed by whatever.

Internally, simp is not treated like most of the remaining flexible tactics, since the distinction is made that simp and simp only, even though they are based on the same tactic, they are different from the perspective of the linter:

  • simp is flexible, while
  • simp only is a "morally" a stopper, but technically it is a "manual exception".
Producing an API that allows to make such a fine distinction would be pretty tricky, short of exposing a Syntax -> Bool predicate to be filled in by the user, which seems unwieldy.
Maybe, for most use-cases, simply being able to add a new tactic to the flexible list and no other frills is enough?

Damiano Testa said:

Allowing a tactic to be considered flexible can be relatively straightforward: move the current list of flexible tactics from being an internal definition, to something stored in an environment extension that the linter can access and the users can modify...

Maybe, for most use-cases, simply being able to add a new tactic to the flexible list and no other frills is enough?

This is what I had in mind and seems a good balance of usefulness/complexity to expose downstream.

Thanks @Damiano Testa for the complete explanation, I hadn't thought of the subtlety although it is clear now you explain it. For all the use cases I have encountered, what you suggest (simply being able to add a new tactic to the flexible list) would be a perfect solution.
